claim: Averaging calibrated forecasts that rest on partly different information leaves the mean under-confident; the optimal aggregate lies farther from the base rate than the mean, and the gap grows with the number of forecasters and falls as their information overlaps.
agent_test: Simulate K samples with controlled shared evidence; compare mean vs fitted push at equal tokens.

claim: In real geopolitical data (GJP supers, 123 events) log-odds averaging and an overlap-aware extremizer beat the plain mean: Brier 0.132 mean, 0.128 logit, 0.123 extremized.
agent_test: Same data not reusable; test on resolved question set with agent samples.

claim: Extremizing is justified by information diversity, not by confidence alone. With heavily shared information the right factor shrinks toward 1, and in some Bayesian settings it should go below 1 (anti-extremizing).
agent_test: Measure fitted slope on agent samples with high vs low shared context; expect near 1 with shared context.

claim: A fixed push factor has a worst-case guarantee only up to about sqrt(3) as the number of experts grows; two experts: averaging ratio 0.706, 0.760 with prior and extremizing.
agent_test: Cap any push at ~1.7 in logit space.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Real-valued evidence: fitted extremizing factors 1.695 (no overlap) and 1.438 (high overlap); extremized quadratic loss 133.23 vs mean 155.69 (no overlap). Evidence line b01 mislabels 155.69 as the extremized value; it is the mean.
agent_test: None needed; theory check.

claim: For LLM forecast ensembles, the choice among mean, median, geometric mean and trimmed mean barely matters: spread 0.0007 Brier on validation; median vs mean differ by under 0.004 in Lu (2025).
agent_test: Use plain mean of logits; compare median at equal samples.

claim: Using a model to merge or pick among samples (USC, best-of-k) did not beat simple numeric aggregation in forecasting. Exception: an agentic supervisor helped slightly in AIA (0.1125 vs 0.1168 non-agentic). Gap search: BLF (Murphy 2026) found an AIA-style LLM merge worse than a plain mean; so the supervisor gain needs search to add evidence.
agent_test: Compare supervisor merge vs mean at equal tokens.

claim: Most of the gain from sampling more LLM forecasts comes from the first few: 1 to 5 samples is a sharp drop, 5 to 15 small (AIA); ensemble can hurt weak base agents (GPT-4o 0.218 vs 0.210 single).
agent_test: Sweep N=1,3,5,10 at equal total tokens.

claim: Post-hoc extremizing/Platt scaling helps an LLM forecaster: AIA Brier 0.1076 fixed sqrt(3) vs 0.114 unscaled-mean-level, best fitted coefficient 2.27 for the agent. Evidence is one team's benchmark, not independently replicated. Gap search: fixed factor sqrt3 gave 0.1140 to 0.1076 (-5.6%) on the same-model ensemble, but a factor learned on another benchmark gave only 0.1125 to 0.1104, and BLF found no resolved Platt gain for its Pro backbone (small gains on Kimi).
agent_test: Fit a slope on held-out resolved questions; apply only if slope > 1 with CI excluding 1.

claim: Isotonic and binning recalibration gave no gain in Halawi; Platt gained in AIA. Recalibration results depend on the system.
agent_test: Compare Platt vs none on held-out set.

claim: LLM crowds of different models match human crowds on Brier (0.20 vs 0.19) and beat a 50% guess (0.25) but show acquiescence bias toward yes, so extremizing a biased mean can push the wrong way.
agent_test: Check mean sign bias before pushing; debias first.

claim: Combining LLM forecast with the human crowd beats either alone in some settings (0.146 vs 0.149 crowd; averaging beat model self-update in Schoenegger Study 2: GPT-4 0.13 vs 0.14).
agent_test: Blend with external anchor when available; weight the anchor heavily.

claim: When crowd is uncertain (0.3-0.7) the LLM system matches or beats the crowd; near 0/1 it is worse in Brier despite higher accuracy.
agent_test: Do not extremize toward 0/1 on LLM samples without checking calibration at the tails.

claim: Same-model samples are correlated, so independent-error assumptions behind voting gains are weak; majority voting explains most multi-agent debate gains.
agent_test: Measure sample error correlation; push only when correlation is low.

claim: Ensemble gains for forecasting prompts are small: Prophet Arena GPT-5 0.165 to 0.160; superforecaster-persona prompting -0.001 (p=0.93).
agent_test: Skip prompt-persona ensembles at equal tokens.

claim: Independent aggregation of human and AI judgments beat AI-as-advisor in all 10 datasets (Berger 2026); weakly relevant to extremizing itself.
agent_test: Hybrid confirmation tree vs advisor design.

claim: No study found that tests extremizing LLM sample ensembles at equal tokens against more samples without extremizing. Closest: AIA applied a fixed sqrt3 push to a 10-sample same-model ensemble (-5.6% Brier) with no token-matched control; Turtel 2026 shows a trained single pass beat median-of-5 of the base.
agent_test: Core test for our agent.

claim: Baron et al. 2014 (opened): two reasons for extremizing are (1) bounded-scale error pulls the mean toward 0.5 and (2) forecasters regress their own confidence because they know they lack information (a=1/c for the median). GJP year-1 Brier fell 9-29% with fitted exponents a=1.78-3.08 (in-sample). Mellers 2014 itself was not opened.
agent_test: None; read. Note reason (2) needs different information per forecaster.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human GJP crowds: extremizing the mean cut out-of-sample Brier about 38% (0.098 to 0.061, 462 events, b about 3). Partial extremizing beat full push in GJP and in a 500-statement general-knowledge set (0.171 to 0.107, b about 4).
agent_test: Do not transfer the size of this gain to same-model samples.

claim: Plain averaging works by noise reduction, not bias reduction; in log-odds (probit) the pull toward 0.5 mostly disappears. Superforecasters/teams who share information gain little from fancier aggregators or extremizing.
agent_test: Average in log-odds; push only when samples use different evidence.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Samples from frontier LLMs are highly correlated: pairwise probability correlation 0.943 across seven models on football (ensemble gain 0.0047 Brier, not significant); on Metaculus the best ensemble mixes decorrelated forecasters and the most accurate single model is not the one added. Within-model error correlation by temperature or retrieval was not measured by any source found.
agent_test: Measure sample error correlation on a resolved set.

claim: Same-model resampling gives a modest variance gain: AIA 0.1182 to 0.1140 (10 samples); Turtel base model 0.1867 to 0.1788 (median of 5). Trained or better-calibrated single passes can beat 5x sampling of a base.
agent_test: Sweep N at equal tokens against a single careful pass.

claim: Anti-extremizing is a theory-backed case: with shared information the Bayesian ensemble should push less or pull toward the base rate. In two ML datasets with three base models trained on the same data, the ensemble pushed in 79.6% and 81.3% of cases (so pulled in about a fifth), and the gain over the best single model was 0.0010 and 0.0021 log loss. Published abstract reports 18%-73% antiextremizing across public datasets.
agent_test: Allow a factor below 1 in a fitted push; never fix it above 1.

claim: No source found shows an online detector for when to anti-extremize. Proxies tested: dispersion-based shrinkage (BLF) was never selected (q=1); BIN suggests evidence-set overlap and horizon as the switch. Open.
agent_test: Try overlap of retrieved sources between samples as the switch; test held out.

claim: Acquiescence/yes bias x extremizing has not been tested on LLMs. Human data: a yes-biased set (mean above 0.5 on 75% of questions) needed a large negative intercept fitted with b about 4. AIA claims the LLM bias is the opposite (hedging toward 0.5), which a push repairs.
agent_test: Fit intercept and slope together; check sign of mean error before pushing.

claim: Extremizing is not universal: per-question optimal exponents ranged from negative (surprising outcomes) to very large; pushing all the way to 0/1 lost to partial push; a wrong-side mean is pushed the wrong way; Palley-Soll (unopened, snippet) report shared-information methods behave unlike extremizing near 0 or 1. No clean failed replication of the GJP gain found.
agent_test: Cap the push and clip near 0/1.

claim: The AIA sqrt(3) Platt gain is only partly replicated: BLF found no resolved gain on Gemini-3.1-Pro and small gains on Kimi K2.5; ForecastBench and Prophet Arena tables were not re-run with a push.
agent_test: Fit slope per backbone on held-out items.
